Friday is IPO day for SpaceX. There's been no shortage of hype and breaking
news around Elon Musk, the world's richest man, taking SpaceX
([SPCX](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/SPCX.O/)) public. Let's talk
about what it means for retirees, investors, and everyone else.

Due to SpaceX's current, sky-high, $1.77 trillion
[valuation](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-ipo-how-
to-buy-before-june-12-140548493.html), set to be finalized Thursday, the
company's initial public offering has broad implications for all of us,
including those who don't invest in the markets. This market entry will touch
pensions, 401(k)s, and the broader economy in unpredictable ways.

Unlike traditional mega-cap IPOs, SpaceX lost billions in the year before
filing to bring the company public. In fiscal year 2025, SpaceX posted [a net
loss of $4.94 billion](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/msci-
confirms-early-index-inclusion-rules-ahead-spacex-ipo-2026-06-08/), and xAI,
which Musk merged with SpaceX in February 2026, [lost $6.36
billion](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/financials-look-
reckless-lifting-xai-000608351.html) that same year.

In terms of the company valuation Musk and his underwriting banks have arrived
at, investment research firm Morningstar has shared that it would shave that
down by [about 56%](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/03/morningstar-spacex-ipo-
target-price-nasdaq.html).

Given that a 2024 _[Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/business/elon-
musk-illegal-drugs-e826a9e1)_[ story](https://www.wsj.com/business/elon-musk-
illegal-drugs-e826a9e1) ran with the subhead, "Some executives and board
members fear the billionaire's use of drugs - including LSD, cocaine, ecstasy,
mushrooms and ketamine - could harm his companies," what does it mean that
this country's financial systems are turning themselves into propulsion
systems to ensure that Musk becomes a trillionaire this Friday?
